learning_outcomes.text: Understand the basic units, quantities and technologies in telecommunications.
Identify and apply tasks in the field of communication technology.

syllabus_topics: Simplex and duplex communication (radio, television x telephone)
Concepts of backbone and access network
Signaling and synchronization in communication networks
Effect of capacitance imbalance on line transfer function
Advantages and disadvantages of aerial optical paths, LASER and LED connectors
The principle of light transmission by fiber optic
Spectral attenuation characteristic of opt fibers
Spectrum of semiconductor light sources for opt
Basics of radio signal propagation, radiocommunications chain, overview of radio channel systems (Wifi-BT-Wimax-Zigbee)
TCP/IP model and architecture, relationship to RM OSI model
MAC address, IPv4 and IPv6 addresses
Networks active elements - HUB, switch router, fundamentals of routing (routing protocols - RIP, OSPF, BGP)
Advanced services in networking - DHCP, NAT, DNS
1st and 2nd generation mobile networks (overview) - 3rd and 4th generation mobile networks (UMTS, LTE)
Data mobile networks (HSCSD, GPRS, EDGE, HSPA, LTE)
The role of cryptography and the cryptographic system
Overview of ciphers and algorithms, hash functions and digital signature
Future of cryptography - quantum key distribution
Protocols suitable for real-time transmission of information
Codecs for voice and quality transmission parameters
Video, Color models - RGB, CMY, CMYK, YUV
HD, Full HD and UHD resolution
Picture and video processing options, compression, formats and containers
The concept of the Internet of things

Description of technology and used transmission networks, principles of information transfer in IoT infrastructure, introduction to protocols and usage possibilities, overview of hardware and functional possibilities
bibliography: T. Anttalainen, J. Ville: Introduction to Communication Networks, Artech House Communications and Network Engineering Series, 367 p., 2014.
M. Clark: Networks and Telecommunications, John Wiley & Sons, Ltd, 2nd edition, 973 p., 2001.
